name: Dido
notes: Downtempo adult pop with a programmed bed under a plain-spoken vocal: 88–100 straight with a 16th hat and the backbeat on 2&4. The harmonic signature is documented and is what this model exists to carry — minor verses resolving to the relative major for the chorus, "i–VI–III–VII in the verse resolving to I–V–vi–IV in the chorus" — so both cycles are authored as families of equal weight and the scales carry both modes. Three drum deltas are quoted: "kick on 1 and the '&' of 3", "soft snare/clap on the backbeat" with the whole kit "low in the mix" (a velocity tier well under the parent's and a `gainOffsetDb` of −7 on the percussion), and "16th filtered hat" with "vinyl-noise and tambourine as texture". The bass is stated as *programming* rather than playing — "a rounded sub on roots, long notes, no slides" — which is `mirror_kick` at 0.96 with `glideProb` 0.01. The melody is given as a range and a habit: "conversational, narrow (A3–C5), sits mostly on chord tones", so the register is 57–72 with `chordToneBias` at 0.88, the highest here. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are the drum probabilities and the velocity tier — "low in the mix" is a direction and 84/58/24 is this author's reading of it. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“bass *programming* rather than played bass on most tracks — a rounded sub on roots, long notes, no slides; live bass appears only for the choruses.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
